lines.text: This hope only faded with the period when man began to
suppose that by knowledge and technical science he could
wholly subjugate the world to his own dominion. We are
now living in this age, and indeed we are at its climax since
we not only understand how to organize and exploit the
powers of nature by technical mastery, but also suppose that
we can control the life of man by means of an ingeniously
contrived and subtly elaborated technique designed to
ensure complete dominance over the minds of men. Thus it
is hoped to establish an empire of success.
How in such circumstances shall our vision penetrate
beyond this visible world into the realm of the eternal and
invisible? How should we lift up our eyes to the hills whence
comes our help, since we expect all needed help to flow from
our own insight and power of accomplishment? How should
we still hope for the end of this world and its ways? How
should we still be able to ask the question concerning the
One who is to come? But this is the mind of Christians, that
they suffer in face of the world and its woes. Not that they
withdraw themselves from the world, or refuse gratefully to
receive the world's gifts, or to co-operate in the work of the
world with a full sense of responsibility. But it is well that
they realize that all this world's gifts and demands cannot
make a man happy within, nor can they in the last resort
claim the surrender of his being. Christians know that in
this world there can be no reign of peace and justice and
pure joy.
How do they know this? They cannot hide from them-
selves the sway which death exercises over the earth, nor
transfigure it with fine-sounding words. They see how
cruelly it often crushes the blossoms of life, and how its
auxiliaries and accomplices, those powers which ravage
youth and health, bring distress and pain to men which
cannot always be removed even by the most advanced
hygiene and medical science. They know that no human
achievement is abiding, and that everything that men create
and build is marked by the curse of decay; that all talk of
